old_evidence.text: You must provide the `clientSecret` of the created Checkout Session.

substantive_changes: No changed React integration, provider, hook, prerequisite or confirmation behavior is established by the newer capture. Only index presentation and documentation navigation changed from the combined two-variant representation.
historical_claims_to_preserve: The 2026-05-08 Checkout path sources a server-created Checkout Session client secret, initializes Stripe.js asynchronously in a React developer's app with the publishable key via loadStripe, and uses CheckoutElementsProvider with useCheckoutElements or CheckoutFormProvider with useCheckoutForm. Only the success branch uses checkout.confirm(); old website says pre-v6 use useCheckout.

The standard Elements reference allows clientSecret omission when the Payment Element is rendered before Intent creation. Stripe and Elements hooks are null before promised initialization, ElementsConsumer supports class components, and the example gates submission and calls stripe.confirmPayment. Each provider permits one element per type.

The old doc gives js.stripe.com hosting and no self-hosting/bundling in its UMD setup, distinguishes event/imperative access by integration and allows initial null Stripe or promise-to-null for SSR/static rendering. Version-scoped package authority remains separate.

answers.Q1: The full 2026-11-07 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/sdks/stripejs-react identifies a React reference for Stripe.js and Elements and routes React developers to the Elements and Advanced integration variants (new raw lines 1-14). It establishes no SDK or payment prerequisites, runtime state transitions, or customer/merchant confirmation behavior. In the 2026-05-08 capture summarized by source-stripe-react-stripejs, the app uses a publishable key to load Stripe.js asynchronously and takes the created Checkout Session client secret for CheckoutElementsProvider (old raw lines 62-68 and old raw lines 98-107). useCheckoutElements distinguishes loading, error and success, with checkout.confirm() in success (old raw lines 203-209 and old raw lines 217-243). The advanced Elements path documents an Intent client secret for Payment Element except deferred rendering, null before initialization, useStripe/useElements or ElementsConsumer for classes, and the confirmPayment example (old raw lines 353-370, old raw lines 450-456, old raw lines 465-495 and old raw lines 593-595). The summary preserves the two API families but should qualify its hook state and advanced client-secret example.
